The top bar is the money that came in. The bar below shows where it went: each category, and what was left over as saved. The two bars use the same scale, so you can compare them directly.

An estimate of how much money your everyday accounts will hold over the next 90 days. Penny starts from today’s balances, adds income it expects, and takes away your upcoming bills and your usual spending pace. If the line goes below zero, you may run short before then. Pick a category below and slide it to see how cutting back would change the picture. It is a guide, not a promise.

resources.string: A spending limit is the most you want to spend on one kind of thing each period: food, rent, travel, fun. Set an amount and Penny shows how much is left as you spend, warns you before you reach it, and lets you move money from one limit to another if one runs out. Some apps call these envelopes, like cash kept in labelled envelopes.
Can’t find it? Type a name above to add it.

No account and no server. Penny saves your changes, encrypted, in a folder you choose. Keep that folder the same on your other phones and tablets with a free sync app such as Syncthing, or a Google Drive or OneDrive folder-sync app. Only your recovery phrase can open the files.
On another device, install Penny, open Sync, choose the same folder and type your recovery phrase.
Write these 24 words down and keep them safe. You need them to open this folder on another device, and to restore an encrypted backup. Penny cannot show them again.
This folder already has Penny data from another device. Type the 24-word recovery phrase you wrote down there.

No account and no server. Penny keeps this book, encrypted, in a folder of its own that you share with the others, for example a Syncthing folder or a shared Google Drive or OneDrive folder kept in sync by an app. You get a 24-word share code to give them.

That folder already has Penny files. Choose a new, empty folder just for this book.

To add someone: share the folder with them, then give them the share code in person or by message. On their phone they open Shared spaces and tap Join a shared book. Everyone with the code can read and change this book.
Give these 24 words only to the people you share this book with. Anyone with the folder and these words can read and change it. This is not your personal recovery phrase.
Someone shared a book with you? Choose the shared folder their sync app keeps on this phone, then type the share code they gave you.
